discover.summary: Describe the engine: game rules, conventions, limits, the operations this session may call (with examples) and error codes. Pass `operation` for one operation's full schemas.

session.status.summary: Report this session's role, revision, open project, active episode and snapshots.

project.create.summary: Open a new, empty in-memory project (replacing any open project; unsaved changes are discarded).

project.load.summary: Open a project file. Invalid or incompatible files are rejected without changing the session.

project.save.summary: Write the open project to a file atomically (temporary file, fsync, rename).

scene.create.summary: Create a scene from an ASCII layout or from width/height, with optional rules.

scene.get.summary: Return a scene with every entity (including labels), its rules, ASCII view and digest.

scene.validate.summary: Check completeness (player, exit) and gameplay problems (unsolvable, too slow for max_ticks, unusable keys or doors).

scene.apply_batch.summary: Apply create/update/remove/update_rules edits atomically: all succeed, or the scene and revision stay unchanged and the failing edit index is reported.

scene.update_rules.summary: Change rule parameters (max_ticks, win_condition) of a scene.

scene.render.summary: Render a scene as SVG (entity ids labelled) or ASCII, inline or to a file. For human inspection; no GUI needed.

entity.create.summary: Create one entity; the engine assigns its id.

entity.get.summary: Return one entity, including its authoring label.

entity.update.summary: Change an entity's kind, position and/or label (empty label clears it).

entity.remove.summary: Remove an entity. Its id is never reused.

analysis.reachability.summary: Answer whether a target (default: the win condition) is reachable from a start (default: the player spawn), separately for walls only (geometric) and under the full rules (gameplay); when it is not, list the blockers and verified single-removal repairs.

episode.start.summary: Start a new episode (replacing the active one) on a frozen copy of a scene; later scene edits do not affect it.

episode.reset.summary: Start a new episode from the active episode's frozen starting scene.

episode.observe.summary: Return the player's observation of the active episode, including legal actions.

episode.act.summary: Submit one action and advance exactly one tick. Rejected actions change nothing and explain why.

episode.events.summary: Return the most recent events of the active episode, optionally only after a tick.

episode.assert.summary: Evaluate assertions (outcome, position, keys, tick bound, event occurrence) against the active episode.

snapshot.capture.summary: Capture the open project and active episode (simulation state only) in memory.

snapshot.restore.summary: Restore a snapshot's project and episode. The revision still increases, so writes based on older revisions stay stale.

replay.export.summary: Export the active episode's replay: initial scene, accepted actions and per-tick hashes. Authors may pass a path; players write to the launcher's replay directory or receive it inline.

replay.verify.summary: Re-execute a replay's recorded actions and compare every state hash and the outcome; optionally check it belongs to a scene of the open project.

oneOf.description:
Trusted: may create, inspect and modify projects, scenes and entities, run analysis,
snapshots and replay verification, and also play episodes.

Restricted: may only play episodes of the scene the launcher chose, observe them and
export their replays. Cannot change rules, spawn entities, set state or restore.

EntityId.description:
Stable identifier of an entity within one scene.

Identifiers are handed out in strictly increasing order by the scene's [`IdAllocator`]
and are never reused, even after the entity is removed. An ID quoted in a diagnostic,
event or replay therefore denotes exactly one entity in that scene's history.

Position.description:
A cell coordinate. `x` grows east, `y` grows south, `(0, 0)` is the north-west corner.

Coordinates are signed so that out-of-range requests deserialize and can be rejected
with a precise `out_of_bounds` error instead of an opaque type error.

Episode ids are never reused (reset, start and restore all issue new ones).

expected_tick.description:
If given, the action is rejected (`stale_tick`) unless the episode is at this tick.
Together with `expected_episode_id` this makes retries exactly-once.
